title: Looking for investors who know a company well enough to challenge an AI research report
author: TheDueDiligent
selftext:
I’m building ThesisCheck, a research tool that takes an investment thesis and checks its individual claims against company filings and other dated sources.

I’m looking for around ten experienced investors who would be interested in testing it on companies they already know well.

The most useful feedback would come from people who can spot things such as:

* important evidence the report missed
* claims that were framed incorrectly
* filing excerpts that were misunderstood
* weak or outdated sources
* dilution, governance, or funding issues that should have been surfaced
* conclusions that go further than the evidence supports

The report breaks the thesis into separate claims and marks each one as supporting, contradicting, or not found, with the underlying sources attached.

I’ll provide two full checks to start. Anyone who sends detailed feedback can receive another 8–13 checks.

You would be a good fit if you regularly read company filings, annual reports, earnings materials, or other primary sources.

Please comment or message me with:

1. How long you have researched individual companies
2. The sectors or markets you know best
3. One company you know particularly well
4. A link to any research you have published, if applicable

There is no requirement to post a review or testimonial. I’m mainly looking for thoughtful feedback from investors who are willing to point out where the research falls short.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The quality of your data source is everything when analyzing stocks. Free APIs like Yahoo Finance or Alpha Vantage are way too shallow for serious decisions they lack depth on fundamentals, insider transactions, and accurate historical ratios. You need a paid feed like Polygon or Intrinio to get reliable financials. That said, even with good data, you still need a model to interpret it. That is why [trademates.co](http://trademates.co) is better than other solutions it replaces the need for an expert opinion by using a 30 year PE investing framework and Claude to score any stock on a 90 day horizon, with community signal showing what others are analyzing right now.

replies.author: TheDueDiligent
replies.body: That’s a different product. And TradeMates’ own site lists Finnhub and Yahoo Finance as its data sources... It generates a 90-day Buy/Hold/Avoid opinion. ThesisCheck does not claim to replace expert judgment or predict returns. Instead, it tests a user’s thesis against primary filings and dated sources, then exposes support, contradictions, and missing evidence. This post is specifically asking knowledgeable investors to identify where that evidence work fails.

replies.author: tradematesHQ
replies.body: You’re right that data sources matter, but even with premium feeds, an investor who spent 30 years at Microsoft still can’t predict a stock’s future better than market data and insider sentiment. The only edge that experienced investor has over the data is gut feeling — and after almost a decade as a PE investor, I’ve learned that gut feeling is worth less than what insider transactions and financials actually show. That’s why [trademates.co](http://trademates.co) scores stocks on a 90-day horizon using market data and insider sentiment rather than any single person’s opinion.
